title: The Potter and the Clay

questions.question: Where did the Lord tell Jeremiah to go down to, where he would let him hear his words?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:2 (ESV): "Arise, and go down to the potter's house, and there I will let you hear my words."

questions.question: What was the potter doing when Jeremiah arrived?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:3 (ESV): "So I went down to the potter's house, and there he was working at his wheel."

questions.question: When the vessel the potter was making of clay was spoiled in his hand, what did he do?
options: He reworked it into another vessel
questions.correctAnswer: He reworked it into another vessel
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:4 (ESV): "And the vessel he was making of clay was spoiled in the potter's hand, and he reworked it into another vessel, as it seemed good to the potter to do."

questions.question: "O house of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter has done? declares the Lord. Behold, like the... in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Israel."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:6 (ESV): "Behold, like the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Israel."

questions.question: "If at any time I declare concerning a nation or a kingdom, that I will pluck up and break down and destroy it, and if that nation, concerning which I have spoken, turns from its..., I will relent of the disaster that I intended to do to it."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:7-8 (ESV): "and if that nation, concerning which I have spoken, turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I intended to do to it."

questions.question: "And if at any time I declare concerning a nation or a kingdom that I will build and plant it, and if it does evil in my sight, not... my voice, then I will relent of the good that I had intended to do to it."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:9-10 (ESV): "and if it does evil in my sight, not listening to my voice, then I will relent of the good that I had intended to do to it."

questions.question: "Now, therefore, say to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: 'Thus says the Lord, Behold, I am shaping... against you and devising a plan against you. Return, every one from his evil way...'"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:11 (ESV): "Behold, I am shaping disaster against you and devising a plan against you."

questions.question: When told to return from their evil ways, what did the people of Judah say?
options: "That is in vain! We will follow our own plans."
"Let the Lord do as he pleases."
"Who are you to tell us this?"
questions.correctAnswer: "That is in vain! We will follow our own plans."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:12 (ESV): "But they say, 'That is in vain! We will follow our own plans, and will every one act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart.'"

questions.question: "Therefore thus says the Lord: Ask among the nations, Who has heard the like of this? The virgin Israel has done a very... thing."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:13 (ESV): "The virgin Israel has done a very horrible thing."

questions.question: "Does the snow of Lebanon leave the crags of Sirion? Do the mountain waters run dry, the cold flowing streams? But my people have... me; they make offerings to false gods;"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:14-15 (ESV): "But my people have forgotten me; they make offerings to false gods;"

questions.question: "...making their land a horror, a thing to be... at forever. Everyone who passes by it is horrified and shakes his head."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:16 (ESV): "making their land a horror, a thing to be hissed at forever."

questions.question: "Like the... wind I will scatter them before the enemy. I will show them my back, not my face, in the day of their calamity."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:17 (ESV): "Like the east wind I will scatter them before the enemy."

questions.question: Who said, "Come, let us make plots against Jeremiah, for the law shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet"?
options: The men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:18 (ESV): "Then they said, 'Come, let us make plots against Jeremiah... Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and let us not pay attention to any of his words.'" (Context implies the rebellious people/leaders).

questions.question: Jeremiah prayed: "Is evil a recompense for good? Yet they have dug a... for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak good for them..."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:20 (ESV): "Yet they have dug a pit for my life."

questions.question: Jeremiah prayed against his enemies: "Therefore deliver up their children to..., give them over to the power of the sword; let their wives become childless and widowed."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 18:21 (ESV): "Therefore deliver up their children to famine, give them over to the power of the sword;"

key_verse_text: "O house of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter has done? declares the Lord. Behold, like the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Israel."
